Thanks teacher Claire Show less Read more Like 1 Dislike ❤ by @EnglishTeacherClaire Reply @maxzile4860 10 months ago (edited) Morning by the Rhone The early sun spilled soft gold across the veranda of a quiet old house by the Rhône. A light breeze drifted through the grapevines as Lily, her blonde hair tied loose, stood barefoot and cradled her saxophone like an old friend. She played softly — a wandering, lazy melody — her notes curling like mist over the river. The melody was Candy Dulfer’s; Lily was here. Max stepped out of the house, careful not to disturb the rhythm. In one hand, he held a steaming cup of coffee; in the other, a tiny glass with 50 ml of plum brandy. “Your usual,” he said gently, setting the tray down beside her wicker chair. Lily lowered the sax and smiled. “You spoil me, Max.” He shrugged with a grin. “I figure if you're going to greet the river with jazz, you deserve the proper fuel.” She picked up the glass, held it to the light. “You know,” she said playfully, “this is almost as apple cider vinegar in water. Some swear it’s good for the circulation.” Max raised an eyebrow. “That’s a strange comparison.” She laughed lightly. “No stranger than plum brandy before breakfast.” He leaned on the wooden railing beside her. “Well, you make it seem elegant. Besides... the way you play in the morning? That melody is healthier than any diet.” Lily looked at him — really looked — and for a brief moment, the air felt warmer. “Careful, Max,” she said, sipping the brandy slowly. “You’re starting to sound like the saxophone.” Show less Read more Like 1 Dislike Reply @中村哲博-d2h 9 months ago Shohei Ohtani is as talented as any player in baseball.
